policy_notes.title: Protect College Sports Act reaches the Senate floor (The Athletic, Sept 24)
policy_notes.body: The bipartisan bill was approved for a Sept 28 final Senate vote — the day this edition publishes. It would create a limited NCAA antitrust exemption, retain House-era direct sharing, add a $22.5M retention pool plus a $5M non-revenue/women's-sports pool (a near-$50M per-school ceiling), preempt certain state NIL laws, and route outside-entity deals through a NIL Go approval framework. Senate passage alone is not enactment — the House must still pass it.

policy_notes.title: Conference 'Plan B' framework (Yahoo Sports, Sept 27)
policy_notes.body: Conference executives are reported to be developing an alternative framework modeled partly on the federal bill, including a harder $48.8M revenue-share cap. Reported planning, not enacted policy.

policy_notes.title: CSC mechanics in force today (College Sports Commission)
policy_notes.body: The published 2026-27 revenue-sharing cap is ~$21.58M per school; direct payments must be reported through CAPS within five business days; third-party NIL sits outside the institutional cap; scholarship-related overages can draw a $0.20-per-$1 fine up to $2.5M. No new CSC clearinghouse release or enforcement action was verifiable in the Sept 21-28 window.
